notes: Tesla Giga Texas Optimus factory (not a facility row): the basenor article (published 2026-06-19, updated 2026-07-16) places a 10 million units per year factory on the 'North Campus' of Giga Texas and targets 'meaningful output ... Summer 2027', but the page names no city or state, and its $5 to $10 billion figure comes from unnamed industry reports. Source: https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-breaks-ground-on-10m-year-optimus-factory-at-giga-texas . A city-stated source would be needed to add a row.

Apptronik / Jabil (skipped, no city): the February 2025 partnership is confirmed by search results only, and no opened page names a production city. Apptronik's Austin base is its headquarters, not a stated plant location.

Hyundai / Boston Dynamics US production plant (skipped, no city): Manufacturing Dive (2026-09-22) says the planned US robot plant could build 30,000 robots per year and that 'A location was not disclosed.' Savannah is a test and training center, included as a facility row.

ABB Auburn Hills, Michigan (skipped, page not opened): the ABB press release timed out on three fetches, and the automate.org copy returned HTTP 403 or 429. Search snippets describe a Michigan Business Development Program grant of $450,000 for a 72-job expansion, a $20 million expansion, and a refit that opened in 2024. These are unverified leads, not citable rows, and should be re-fetched later.

FANUC Michigan plant (skipped, no city on an opened page): the FANUC press release (opened) says 'New 840,000 sq. ft. Michigan site', $90 million, 225 jobs, late 2027 completion, and is datelined Rochester Hills, MI (the HQ). Local outlets (dbusiness, manufacturing.net) name Pontiac, MI, but both returned HTTP 403, so Pontiac is unverified. A search snippet cites a Michigan Strategic Fund grant of $1.575 million. Re-fetch the local coverage to place the city.

KUKA US robot assembly (no plant found): search results found no confirmed US KUKA robot assembly plant. KUKA's US operations are in Michigan (sales, support, integration). A competitor's 2025 guide says production is in Germany, Hungary and China, but that is marketing content and was not verified.

Wistron Fort Worth status: the Hillwood page (opened, 2025-08-22) describes the two plants as announced and planned. A search snippet claims the D1 factory already produces NVIDIA GB300 superchips, but the DataCenterDynamics page returned HTTP 403, so this stays unverified and the status is set to announced.

Foxconn Houston: a Foxconn-led AI supercomputer component plant in Houston appears only in search snippets. ENR (opened) says Foxconn's subsidiary 'had obtained a 118-acre site in Houston for $33 million', but the article does not link that site to the Apple server plant, so no acreage is recorded for the plant.

Apple Houston: Apple did not name its manufacturer. ENR attributes that to Reuters ('Apple's manufacturer is Foxconn'). The article says the plant is 'scheduled to open next year', and the planned opening year 2026 is inferred from that. No plant-specific investment or job count was stated.

Saronic Franklin: the Naval News date is shown as 03/12/2025 on the page and appears to be early December 2025 from the URL path, so 'published' is recorded as 2025-12 only. The 1,500 jobs and 300,000 sq ft figures are quoted from the same article.

Saronic Port Alpha: the investment is quoted as 'a planned investment of more than $3 billion', and the value is recorded as 3,000,000,000 on that basis. Search snippets report differing figures ($2.5 billion, $5 billion). Port Alpha was placed in Brownsville from the 2026-07-16 article, although a different search snippet still described Louisiana as the site.

Amazon Westborough: the Business Wire release (2021-10-21) returned HTTP 429 and was not opened. The Area Development item (2021-10-29) is used instead, and it gives 200 jobs ('The project is expected to create 200 new jobs') and a product of mobile drive units ('will focus primarily on the manufacturing of Amazon Robotics mobile drive units').

Not researched within budget: Serve Robotics, Zipline, Skydio, Shield AI and Anduril factories (only Saronic was searched). Anduril's Columbus, Ohio plant was excluded by the topic. Hyundai's US robot plant and the Apptronik production site were not placed.

Quote caveat: WebFetch returns a model-processed extract, so several quotes are extracts from the fetch tool's own quoting, not raw page text. Quotes were kept only where the fetch returned an explicitly quoted sentence containing the fact. Re-check each against the live page before publication.
